A.F.M. Abdur Rahman, J: This Rule under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 issued, on 20.2.2002, at the instance of the original defendant Mrs. Rohima Khatoon and her son Md. Abdul Khaleque, is directed against the judgment and decree, dated 01.12.1998, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Bogra, in Other Class Appeal 'No. 108 of 1993, affirming those of dated 17.4.1993, passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra, in Other Class Suit No. 112 of 1984, decreeing the Suit. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the rule the petitioner obtained an order of stay against the operation of the judgment and decree, dated, 01.10.1998, passed in Other Class Appeal No. 108 of 1993 for six months which was further extended till disposal of this rule. 

 7. The learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra, upon hearing the evidence adduced by the parties and considering the materials on record passed his judgment on 17.4.1993 through which the suit was decreed and the defendant No. 1- was directed to execute the sale deed within 15 days, in default the plaintiff was made entitled to get the sale deed executed and registered through the Court. 

 8. As against the said judgment and decree, dated 17.4.1993, the defendant No. I preferred Title Appeal No. 108 of 1993 before the District Judge, Bogra, which was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Court No. 2, Bogra, who upon considering the evidence on record and other materials, disallowed the appeal by his judgment, dated 01.12.1998, affirming the judgment passed by the trial Court. 

 18. The learned Advocate Mr. Zahedul Bari, argued that the discretion can only be exercised infavour of a person who is honest and approached the Court with clean hand. But since the petitioner came to this Court with unclean hand by suppressing a further fact that in the meantime the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra, has executed the saf kabala and registered the same and the decree is now awaiting only for execution for handing over the possession of the suit property the attitude of the petitioner disentitled her to get the discretion to be exercised in her favour. 

 19. The learned Advocate Mr. Zahedul Bari, contends that the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner has paid the huge amount of money in the year 1981 to the defendants for purchase of the suit property and obtained decree at the trial Court upon evidence proved before the said court and affirmed by the appellate Court and nowhere the defendant raised any ground of hardship, and therefore this Court cannot consider the question of hardship which actually a non-existent and created ground. The learned Advocate Mr. Zahedul Bari, prays for discharge of the rule. 

 26. The trial court upon finding that the defendant admittedly executed the Bainapatra upon receiving Baina money, decreed the suit and directed the defendants to execute the saf kabala. The appellate Court on consideration of the evidence, available on the record, affirmed the judgment. Both the courts below found that the defendant No. 1, Rohima Khatoon since admittedly executed the Bainapatra is liable under the law to finalize the sale and accordingly decreed the suit and the Appellate Court affirmed the same. 

 30. This prayer clearly indicates that non Specific performance of impugned Bainapatra would not have caused any prejudice to the plaintiff. On the other hand it goes without question that hardship will follow if a person is evicted from his residential house which led the legislature to Promulgate the Provision of Section 6 in the Land Reforms Ordinance 1984 providing the residential house of judgment debtor from being attached or dispossession in execution of a decree which runs as follows; 

 The facts are exactly on all fours with the present- case. There also her husband made a contract for selling his dwelling house and soon thereafter he died, the plaintiff brought the suit for specific performance in 1970. The consideration was Tk. 21,000/- and advance was paid Tk. 3,000/, Since the deed of sale was not executed the suit was filed. The defence was mainly on hardship. The Division Bench carefully considered the defence and concluded. " If we decree the suit, she will be deprived of that income too, for the rest of her life with no shelter to cover her head There can, therefore, be no justification for us to tell her she should sell the house and go on pilgrimage never to return". The Court considered that the plaintiff was a businessman in that case and not a helpless widow like the defendant. In view of those facts, the Court refused to enforce the specific performance no doubt, but appreciated the gesture of the appellant to return the advance amount by three times. This case shows the judicial anxiety to do justice when faced with the similar situation as emphasized in item-II, namely, hardship Vs. hardship, qualified by legal mandate "hardship which he did not foresee vis a-vis no such hardship would accrue to the plaintiff'. 

 "Discretion as to decreeing  specific performance-The-jurisdiction to decree specific performance is discretionary, and the Court is not bound to grant such relief merely because it is lawful to do so; but the discretion of the Court is not arbitrary but sound and reasonable, guided by judicial principles and capable or correction  by a Court a appeal. The following are cases in which the Court may property exercise a discretion not to decree specific performance: 

 The following is a case in which the Court may properly exercise a discretion to decree specific performance:- 

 37. During the pendency of this Rule this court has directed the learned Advocate Ms. Nasrin Ferdous to inform this court that whether her client is ready to pay the compensation at a reasonable amount. But the learned Advocate failed to let this court know about the desire of the petitioners as to the amount of compensation. However since this Court has decided to strike a balance of justice in between the parties, it inclined to divide the property into two parts and to .affirm the decree passed by the court below for 6½ (six and half decimal of land beyond the residential part of the defendant No.1 and to set aside the decree in respect of 6½ (six and half) decimal of land comprised in the residential part of the suit property. 

 40. The decree passed by the courts below for specific performance of the agreement dated 2.2.1981 be reduced to a quantum of land of 6½ (six and half) decimal of land beyond the residential part of the suit property and be ineffective for the 6½ decimal of land comprised in the residential part and the plaintiff-respondent/opposite party shall get compensation at an amount of Tk. 5,00,000.00 (five lacs) for the said 6½ (six and half) decimal of land from the defendants/ Appellants/ Petitioners. The defendants are directed to pay the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of receiving notice from the trial court, in default this rule shall stand discharged.
